measured_state.turn_lifetime_adjudication: MM4's item (1) taken by the coordinator with instruments after that seat wedged at launch. Four questions, all answered from source with the pinned tree, each now a named check in verification/turn_background.py. (A) OUTLIVING: the promotion and the wake lock cannot outlive the turn by two independent bounds - TurnService.finish() is reached on every turn-ending path (Activity.java:265 model result/failure clears turnActive then finishes; :757 stopped; :769 publishReply; :1208 onDestroy) and independently wake.acquire(lease) carries its own timeout while the ticker's 'if(elapsed>=lease){stopSelf();return;}' drives onDestroy, which clears active, removeCallbacksAndMessages, stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE) and release(). Every onStartCommand path returns START_NOT_STICKY, so a killed service is not resurrected without a fresh begin(). (B) STRANDING: cannot happen either, because the lease and the socket deadline are the same window - turnLease (Activity.java:730) = max(30000,min(600000,optLong("timeout_ms",120000))) and the transport deadline for the same effect (:611) = started+max(5000,min(600000,optLong("timeout_ms",120000))); one default (120000), one cap (600000). Pinned by the check 'the promotion window and the request transport window share one default and one cap so the wake lock can neither outlive nor strand the turn'. (C) WHAT SETS THE WINDOW: measured, not assumed - grep of core/ finds exactly one emitter of timeout_ms, core/services.rs:182 (the service/job dispatch; its purpose is a service_request:<ts> ticket), and the model effect (core/application.rs:909, and the hosted-search continuation at :785) carries NO timeout key, so turnLease always resolves to the 120000 default and its 30s-600s clamp never moves. This corrects this ledger's and AUDIT.md's earlier wording that the lease is 'taken from the turn's own request timeout'. Consequence the owner should see: in the shipped Android surface a model request cannot run longer than 120s end-to-end (the same default bounds socket connect, soTimeout and the wake lock), so a provider slower than that is cut off before the lease is the limit. (D) SHARED PROMOTION: yes by design - TurnService.begin reuses the live instance ('if(service!=null&&service.active){service.extend(ticket,started,lease,label);return;}') and onStartCommand re-enters extend() when already active, so a chained model effect (harness retry, hosted-search continuation) rewrites ticket/label/started/lease and re-acquires the lock on the SAME promotion instead of stacking a second one; turnActive is a single volatile boolean, so the Activity never runs two model turns concurrently. (E) REPLY LOSS: the reply is committed to encrypted history before any notification leg, so no conversation data is lost between settle and delivery; what can be lost is the announcement - publishPendingReply is gated by TurnService.notificationsAllowed, so on API 33+ with POST_NOTIFICATIONS denied a backgrounded user gets no signal even though the reply landed (drains: the permission-result callback code==56 and openRequestedConversation on resume). Left as a DEVICE-ACCEPTANCE caveat, not closed here. Not measured: the narrow main-thread race where a begin() lands after the ticker's stopSelf() but before onDestroy (current!=null && active still true -> extend() on a stopping service, so the new turn would run unpromoted); it needs a device or a harness that can order those callbacks, and no source-level instrument can settle it.
